But queens separated by more than one row may share a long diagonal; that is allowed. So adjacency rule: queens cannot be in same row, same column, same region, or adjacent squares (including diagonally). So basically we need a placement of 5 queens on 5x5 board such that each row, column, region has exactly one queen, and no two queens are adjacent (including diagonally). Also no two queens in consecutive rows can be in columns differing by 1 (that's same as adjacency diagonally). But if they are separated by more than one row, they can be on same diagonal (like row 1 col 1 and row 3 col 3). That is allowed.
